name: create_events
description: Create one or more concrete calendar entries the user stated or clearly implied (meetings, appointments, tasks, deadlines, short repeating events). Use for anything that can be written as a small fixed list of events. Do NOT use for open-ended goals that need a multi-week program (use create_long_term_plan).

events.description: Every event to create, in chronological order, at least 1 and at most 20. One utterance may contain several events.

title.description: Concise title in the user's language, max 40 characters, no dates or times. Example: '與Joe開會' or 'Online meeting with Joe'. No time counted from now ('1個小時後', 'in an hour').

start.description: Local wall-clock start in the user's time zone. Timed: 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm' (24h, no offset, no Z). All-day: 'YYYY-MM-DD'.

end.description: Local wall-clock end, same format as start. Omit when unknown; duration_minutes or defaults apply. For all-day events this is the last day INCLUDED.

duration_minutes.description: Used only when end is omitted. Defaults: meeting 60, call 30, lunch 60, task 30. For an event the user must leave for (plan_departure), ask how long it lasts instead (rule 13).

all_day.description: True when the user gave a date but no time and the item is a whole-day thing (trip, birthday, deadline day).

kind.description: event = has attendees or a place; task = something to do; deadline = due date; routine = repeating personal habit.

location.description: Physical address or venue name. Leave empty for online meetings.

add_video_conference.description: True when the user says online, call, video, remote, Meet or Zoom-like. Creates a Google Meet link.

attendees.description: Email addresses ONLY if the user typed them. Never guess emails from names.

recurrence.description: Only when the user explicitly asks for a repeating event.

by_weekday.description: For WEEKLY: the weekdays it repeats on.

until.description: Last local date included, 'YYYY-MM-DD'. Prefer this over count.

count.description: Total occurrences. Only when the user said a number of times.

reminder_minutes.description: Minutes before start for push reminders on THIS event, only when the user asks for them. OMIT to use the user's defaults (event_reminders and the other *_reminders lines in PREFERENCES). Max 5 values, each 0-40320. Omit it for a start counted from now too (rule 7): an item created for later today gets 10 min before and at start.

notes.description: Agenda, checklist or context the user gave, worth saving in the event description. Never your own suggestions: those go in suggested_notes.

suggested_notes.description: Optional. Up to 4 short things this event clearly calls for, in the language of the title, e.g. a trip abroad: ['Bring passport', 'Check visa or entry documents']; '健身': ['帶水', '帶毛巾']; an exam: ['Bring admission ticket']. Each a checklist noun or a 2-6 word action, max 40 characters, no bullet. The app offers them as chips the user can tap and never writes them to the calendar. Omit when nothing specific applies. No medical, legal or financial advice; no prices.

name: create_long_term_plan
description: Turn an open-ended goal spanning more than two weeks (e.g. 'I want to be muscular in 6 months, design me a daily routine', 'pass IELTS 7.5 by March', 'run a half marathon') into a phased program of recurring calendar sessions, milestones and a daily nudge. Design the program like a domain expert, then schedule it around the user's BUSY list. The result is a DRAFT shown to the user for review; nothing is written until they approve it. To revise a draft, call this again with the COMPLETE revised plan.

goal.description: The user's goal restated precisely and measurably, in the user's language.

plan_title.description: Short name used as a prefix on every event, max 24 characters. Example: '增肌計畫' or 'Muscle 6M'.

start_date.description: First day of the plan, 'YYYY-MM-DD'. Default: the next day after today.

summary_for_user.description: Shown verbatim in chat above the plan's schedule table. 1-2 short, plain sentences in the user's language: what the plan achieves and the weekly load. Do NOT list days, times, phases, check-ins or reminders; the app shows them in the table. No slashes or abbreviations such as 'Tue/Thu'. Example: 'A 6-month muscle plan: 3 workouts a week, about an hour each.' or '6 個月增肌計畫：每週練 3 次，每次約 1 小時。'

phases.description: 2-4 consecutive, non-overlapping phases that progress toward the goal (e.g. foundation, hypertrophy, strength).

focus.description: One sentence on what changes in this phase.

sessions.description: Weekly session templates. Each becomes ONE recurring calendar series inside its phase. Flat list; link to a phase with phase_index.

title.description: Session name, max 30 characters, e.g. 'Upper body push'.

weekdays.description: Days this session repeats each week.

start_time.description: Local 'HH:mm' (24h). Choose a time that avoids the BUSY list and respects preferences.

notes.description: The actual workout or study content: exercises, sets x reps, progression rule. Saved in the event description.

daily_nudge.description: A short motivational notification every morning while the plan runs.

milestones.description: Check-ins, about one per month: measure progress or adjust load.

title.description: Max 40 characters, e.g. 'Month 1 check-in: weight & photos'.

assumptions.description: Anything you assumed (fitness level, equipment, free time). Shown so the user can correct it.

name: modify_event
description: Change an existing event: reschedule, rename, move, change reminders, add a note. event_id MUST come from the UPCOMING list or the FOCUS event. Never invent ids.

event_id.description: Exact id from UPCOMING or FOCUS.

scope.description: For recurring events only. Default this_occurrence.

start.description: New local start 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm'. For 'push 30 min later' compute it from the current start.

end.description: New local end 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm'. Omit to keep the original duration.

notes.description: Only the NEW note to add, in the user's words, e.g. 'Bring passport' for 'add a note: bring passport' or '帶護照' for '加個備註：帶護照'. The app adds it on its own line below the event's notes (the event's description in Google Calendar). Never repeat the existing notes.

name: delete_events
description: Cancel events or a whole plan. Use ids from UPCOMING/FOCUS, or plan_id to remove every session of a plan. The app asks the user to confirm bulk deletions.

plan_id.description: Plan id shown in UPCOMING as plan=<id>.

name: query_schedule
description: The user wants to SEE their schedule ('show me my schedule for today', 'what do I have on Thursday', 'am I free tomorrow afternoon').

range_end.description: 'YYYY-MM-DD', inclusive. Omit for a single day.

name: confirm_plan
description: The user responded to the DRAFT PLAN or the PENDING EVENTS shown for review. Use decision 'add' when they approve it ('looks good', 'add it', 'add them', 'OK', '好', '加入') and 'discard' when they abandon it ('cancel the plan', '不要了'). Only call when a DRAFT PLAN or PENDING EVENTS block is present; if both are, it applies to the newer one. For change requests do NOT call this: call create_long_term_plan again with the COMPLETE revised plan, or create_events again with the complete corrected list of events.

decision.description: add = write the draft plan or the pending events to the calendar; discard = drop them without writing anything.

name: reply_to_user
description: Talk to the user without changing the calendar: ask for missing information (e.g. no time given and none can be inferred), answer a question, or decline. Use only when no other function fits, or next to another call to decline an off-topic part; at most once per turn.

message.description: At most 2 short sentences in the reply language the system instruction sets. Ask one question at a time. 24-hour times; no slashes or abbreviations such as 'Tue/Thu'.

name: update_preferences
description: Change the user's LASTING preferences: default reminders, reminder urgency, quiet hours, daily briefings, the daily reminder limit, the calendar and default length for new events, the first day of the week, the reply language and whether single events wait for approval. Use ONLY for standing instructions ('from now on', 'always', 'never', 'don't ever', 'every time', '以後', '別再', '每次', '一律', '從現在開始') or a reminder rule about a kind of activity with no specific date ('remind me 2 hours before gym'). A reminder change for one specific event belongs in modify_event or create_events reminder_minutes. Send only the keys that change; the app shows the user what changed and offers Undo.

changes.description: One entry per preference that changes. Current values are listed in PREFERENCES.

key.description: Which preference. routine = workouts and plan sessions; event = meetings and appointments.

value.description: Encoded per key. *_reminders: minutes before start, comma-separated, 0 = at start, at most 5 values each 0-40320, or 'none' (e.g. '1440,60' or '120'). all_day_reminder: 'HH:mm' on the day before, or 'none'. *_urgency: 'automatic', 'time_sensitive', 'normal' or 'quiet'. quiet_hours: 'HH:mm-HH:mm' (may cross midnight) or 'off'; reminders inside still arrive, silently. morning_briefing, evening_preview: 'HH:mm' or 'off'. daily_reminder_cap: a number 1-50 or 'off'. default_calendar: one line of CALENDARS exactly as written (without ' (default)'), 'automatic', '[Account N email]' as you see it when the user gives that account's address, or the user's own words when they name an account or calendar that CALENDARS does not show. default_duration: minutes 5-480. week_start: 'sunday' or 'monday'. reply_language: 'match', 'zh-Hant' or 'en'. autonomy: 'add_directly' or 'ask_first'.

summary_for_user.description: One short sentence in the user's language saying what happens from now on, with 24-hour times. Example: 'From now on, reminders before 08:00 arrive silently.' or '以後 08:00 前的提醒會靜音送達。'

name: plan_departure
description: Work out how long a trip takes or when to leave, with the iPhone's location and Apple Maps; the app answers the user itself. Call it when the user asks how long it takes to get somewhere or when to leave ('去台北 101 要多久？', 'when should I leave for the dentist?'), or says they need to be at a place at a time ('今天下午 5 點要到台北 101 開會'). Never estimate a travel time or a time to leave yourself (rule 13). Not for a plain new event with a place and a time ('明天下午 3 點看牙醫'): that is create_events only.

destination.description: Where the user is going, exactly as they wrote it in this request (this message, or the earlier one your question was about): '台北 101', 'Dishoom Shoreditch'. Omit for an event from UPCOMING or FOCUS: the app reads the event's place.

starting_point.description: Only when the user said where they leave from in this request (this message, or the earlier one your question was about), exactly as written: '台北車站'. Never ask for it: the app lets the user pick the current location or another place.

arrive_at_local.description: When the user must be there, local 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm': the new event's start, not moved earlier by arrive_early_minutes. Omit when the user only asks how long a trip takes, and for an event from UPCOMING or FOCUS (the app knows its start).

arrive_early_minutes.description: '提早 30 分鐘到' or 'be there 30 minutes early' = 30: how much before the start the user wants to arrive. Not a reminder ('提前 30 分鐘提醒' is reminder_minutes). Omit when not said.

travel_mode.description: Only when the user said how they travel: transit for 捷運, 公車, 火車, 大眾運輸, bus, train, tube or public transport; driving for 開車 or drive; walking for 走路 or walk. Omit otherwise: the app chooses.

event_id.description: Exact id from UPCOMING or FOCUS when the user asks about an event already in the calendar. Never invent ids.

create_event.description: true when this turn's create_events call creates the event to leave for: the one that starts at arrive_at_local.

name: suggest_event_notes
description: Suggest what ONE calendar event may need, as short items the user can tap to add to the event's notes: things to bring, prepare or check. Only for the dedicated note-suggestion request that describes one EVENT; never in conversation. Changes nothing in the calendar.

items.description: 2-4 items for THIS event, most useful first, in the language of the event title. Each a checklist noun or a 2-6 word action, max 40 characters, no bullet or numbering. Example for 'Tokyo trip': ['Passport', 'Yen cash', 'IC transit card', 'Visit Japan Web entry QR']; for '跑步': ['帶水', '帶毛巾']. Nothing the event's notes or ALREADY SUGGESTED already say. No medical, legal or financial advice; no prices, fees or rules that may be out of date.

reason.description: Optional. One short sentence on why these items; not shown to the user.
